questions.question: What are the three specification styles available in Robot Framework?

options.text: Keyword-Driven Specification
Behavior-Driven Specification
Object-Oriented Specification
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't have an Object-Oriented Specification style

options.text: Data-Driven Specification
Test-Driven Specification
options.explanation: Test-Driven is not one of Robot Framework's specification styles

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between Keyword-Driven and Behavior-Driven specification styles?

options.text: Keyword-Driven is declarative; Behavior-Driven is imperative
options.explanation: It's the opposite - Keyword-Driven is imperative, Behavior-Driven is declarative

options.text: Keyword-Driven is imperative; Behavior-Driven is declarative
There is no fundamental difference; they are the same
options.explanation: They have fundamental differences in approach and focus

options.text: Keyword-Driven can only be used for testing; Behavior-Driven only for RPA
options.explanation: Both styles can be used for both testing and RPA

questions.question: In Behavior-Driven Specification, what happens to the Given, When, Then, And, and But prefixes in Robot Framework?

options.text: They are required for the test to run
options.explanation: The prefixes are optional and are basically ignored by Robot Framework

options.text: They are basically ignored if a keyword matching the rest of the name is found
They define special execution order
options.explanation: The prefixes don't affect execution order, they are for readability

options.text: They must be defined as separate keywords
options.explanation: They are prefixes to existing keywords, not separate keywords

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Data-Driven Specification in testing?

options.text: To dynamically acquire data from external sources during execution
options.explanation: That's typical for RPA; in testing, data is specifically chosen to cover different scenarios

options.text: To automate the same sequence with different sets of input and expected output data
To generate random test data automatically
options.explanation: Data-Driven Testing uses predefined data sets, not random generation

options.text: To store test results in a database
options.explanation: Data-Driven Specification is about input data variation, not result storage

questions.question: Which specification style is better suited for complex tasks with complex data and why?

options.text: Behavior-Driven, because it uses natural language
options.explanation: Natural language can become less understandable with complex data

options.text: Keyword-Driven, because it enables clear separation between keyword names and argument values
Data-Driven, because it handles all types of data
options.explanation: Data-Driven is for running the same logic with different data sets, not necessarily complex tasks

options.text: Both styles are equally suited for complex tasks
options.explanation: Keyword-Driven is specifically better for complex tasks due to its structure

questions.question:
Looking at this Robot Framework test case:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Verify Login Page
    Open Browser    https://example.com    Chrome
    Input Text    id=username    testuser
    Input Password    id=password    Test123!
    Click Button    id=login-btn
    Page Should Contain    Welcome testuser
    Close Browser
```

What specification style is being used?

options.text: Behavior-Driven Specification
options.explanation: This uses imperative commands without Given/When/Then structure

options.text: Keyword-Driven Specification
Data-Driven Specification
options.explanation: This doesn't use test templates or data variations

options.text: Mixed specification style
options.explanation: This is purely Keyword-Driven style

questions.question:
Consider these two test implementations:

**Implementation A:**
```robot
*** Test Cases ***
User Can Purchase Product
    Given user is logged in as "customer"
    And product "laptop" is in the cart
    When user proceeds to checkout
    And enters payment details
    Then order should be confirmed
    And confirmation email should be sent
```

**Implementation B:**
```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Purchase Product Test
    Login As User    customer
    Add To Cart    laptop
    Click Checkout Button
    Fill Payment Form    visa    4111111111111111
    Submit Order
    Verify Order Status    confirmed
    Check Email    order_confirmation
```

Which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Implementation A uses Behavior-Driven style
Implementation B uses Keyword-Driven style
Implementation A is declarative (describes what should happen)
Implementation B is imperative (specifies what actions to perform)
Both implementations would execute exactly the same way
options.explanation: While they might achieve the same result, the keywords and execution would differ

questions.question:
Examine this Robot Framework code:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Validate Calculator Operations
    [Template]    Calculate And Verify
    2 + 2    4
    10 - 5    5
    3 * 4    12
    15 / 3    5
    100 + 200    300

*** Keywords ***
Calculate And Verify
    [Arguments]    ${expression}    ${expected}
    ${result}=    Evaluate    ${expression}
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${result}    ${expected}
```

What specification style is being demonstrated here?

options.text: Keyword-Driven Specification only
options.explanation: This uses Test Templates which is a Data-Driven approach

options.text: Behavior-Driven Specification
options.explanation: There's no Given/When/Then structure or behavior description

options.text: Data-Driven Specification
Mixed Keyword-Driven and Behavior-Driven
options.explanation: This is purely Data-Driven using Test Templates

questions.question: Which of the following test cases correctly demonstrate Behavior-Driven style with proper Robot Framework syntax? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Given system is initialized, When user logs in, Then dashboard is displayed
Given user is on login page, When user enters credentials, Then user sees dashboard
Given product is available, But price is too high, When discount is applied, Then user can purchase
Open Login Page, Enter Credentials user pass, Verify Dashboard Loaded
options.explanation: This is Keyword-Driven style with imperative commands, not Behavior-Driven

questions.question:
A team wants to write acceptance tests that business stakeholders can understand, but implement them using technical keywords. Based on the specification styles, what approach is recommended?

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
User Registration
    Given the registration page is open
    When user registers with email "test@example.com"
    Then account should be created successfully

*** Keywords ***
the registration page is open
    Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}/register    ${BROWSER}
    Wait Until Page Contains Element    id=registration-form

user registers with email "${email}"
    Input Text    id=email    ${email}
    Input Text    id=password    SecurePass123!
    Input Text    id=confirm-password    SecurePass123!
    Click Button    id=submit-registration

account should be created successfully
    Wait Until Page Contains    Registration successful
    Location Should Be    ${BASE_URL}/welcome
```

What is correct about this approach?

options.text: This violates Robot Framework best practices by mixing styles
options.explanation: This is actually a recommended approach - BDD for test cases, KDT for implementation

options.text: Test cases use Behavior-Driven style while keywords use Keyword-Driven implementation
This approach doesn't work in Robot Framework
options.explanation: This is a valid and recommended approach in Robot Framework

options.text: The keywords should also use Given/When/Then prefixes
options.explanation: Keywords implementing BDD steps typically use imperative style
